newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks surge as positive sentiment soars.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks surge as positive sentiment soars.

text.p: South African shares surged on Thursday in an all-time high volume of trade as the market's current bullish mood soared to new heights, dealers said.
The market swiftly ignored early jitters over an overnight fall on Wall Street and rapidly gained ground that it held until the end of trade when it finished at its day highs.
More than 1.111 billion rands worth of shares changed hands setting a new trading record as local and foreign institutions poured into blue chip stocks.
Trade was also boosted by active buying from futures players. The all-share index ended up 59.5 points at 6,863.6 as the industrial index rose 47.0 points to 8,180.4.
The wave of positive sentiment has been kicked off by a surging rand, a strong bond market and a healthy outlook for interest rates.
There was still no stopping the rising rand on Thursday which hit a six-month high against the dollar, as markets awaited a major speech by President Nelson Mandela.

Political sources said Mandela was likely to pledge accelerated implementatation of the government's macro-economic strategy -- which includes relaxation of exchange controls and privatisation -- when he addresses parliament on Friday.

Dealers said they expected little detail in the speech with nost betting any specific plans will be announced by finance minister Trevor Manuel in the March 12 budget. This could pave the way for further share price rises until then.
The golds share market also had a good day as dealers bet that the nervous bullion price was starting to hit bottom and could be poised to launch a rally.
The gold index added 13.7 points to 1,387.4.
